newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean police storm bus to free 34 hostages.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean police storm bus to free 34 hostages.

text.p: South Korean police stormed a bus in Seoul on Thursday to free 34 passengers held hostage for more than an hour by a knife-wielding man, witnesses said.

A dozen riot police wearing bullet-proof vests and brandishing automatic rifles kicked open the bus door and fired teargas before rushing in and seizing the man, identified as Kwon Shin-hong, 55. They bundled him into a nearby police van.
The domestic Yonhap news agency said the man was also carrying a home-made bomb but police could not confirm this report.
Witnesses said the bus driver was injured during the police raid. They said it appeared that no passengers, including eight children, were hurt.

Police said Kwon, who they said earlier was 58, took over the bus at around 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) and ordered the driver to go to the Presidential Blue House after complaining the country was "full of communists", but the driver refused.
The driver eventually parked near a government complex in central Seoul.
Passengers said Kwon appeared mentally unstable.
